newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl denies Germans want nuclear weapons - French TV.
newsitem.headline: Kohl denies Germans want nuclear weapons - French TV.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl has denied in a television interview that a Franco-German defence plan unveiled last month implied that his country wanted nuclear weapons.

France's left-wing opposition has accused the French government of sacrificing national defence sovereignty to the United States and NATO in the confidential Joint France-German Security and Defence Concept leaked last month.

"I must say I didn't understand this dispute at all because I didn't find this text so sensational....It is a development of an existing joint position," Kohl told TF1 television in an interview to be broadcast at seven p.m. (1800 GMT).
"To be quite open, sometimes I hear people suggest that hidden in this text is somehow the idea that the Germans want nuclear weapons. We don't want that at all. And that's final," Kohl said.
The last thing he or the Germans wanted, he said, was to share nuclear weapons.
Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac approved the defence document on December 9 in Nuremberg.
Calling the two countries' security interests inseparable, it says their first commitment is to defend NATO and urges a dialogue on the role of nuclear deterrence in European defence.
"I am very happy that apart from the Americans in the West there are also the French and British closer to us who have nuclear weapons," Kohl said.
"And anyone in France who fears that we want to get nuclear weapons through the back door is talking nonsense. We want to work as closely as possible with France militarily," he said.
